idiom_name: iced Message enum, update(&mut State, Message) -> Task, view(&State)
implementation_notes: Rust's GUI ecosystem converges on the Elm architecture rather than on a store object: iced defines one Message enum (the action type), a pure update(&mut State, Message) -> Task<Message> (the reducer, which returns side effects as tasks instead of performing them inline) and a declarative view(&State) function - the same one-way loop with the runtime's message queue in place of the dispatcher and no shared mutable store. The classic structure survives as three rules: one state tree per application, updates only through messages, views read the state immutably. Prefer this shape for native apps; reach for the yew variant when the target is the browser.
pitfalls: view must not mutate state or send messages while rendering; side effects belong in update, returned as a Task (Command) for the runtime to run.
A single application-wide Message enum with dozens of unrelated variants is the Rust analogue of a mega-reducer; nest per-screen message enums and map them into the parent.
Cloning large state into view models every frame costs; borrow slices and pass references or Cow where the widgets allow it.
Long-running work inside update blocks the runtime - return a Task so the executor can run it off the update path.

variants.name: yew use_reducer / use_reducer_eq with impl Reducible
variants.implementation_notes: yew, Rust's component model for WebAssembly, exposes the pattern through hooks: implement Reducible for an action type (type Action plus reduce(self: Rc<Self>, action)), obtain (state, dispatch) from use_reducer or use_reducer_eq, and publish the pair through a ContextProvider so descendants read the same state - Redux in Rust, scoped to the component tree the provider wraps. use_reducer_eq skips notifications when the state compares equal, which needs a meaningful PartialEq. Prefer this variant for web/WASM targets; a truly global store is still just a provider at the root, not a language-level singleton.
pitfalls: reduce runs during rendering and must stay pure - no side effects, no dispatching from inside the reducer, or yew re-renders unpredictably.
use_reducer_eq only pays off with a correct PartialEq; an always-false or always-true comparison either defeats the optimisation or drops real updates.
State published through context is not a serializable history; persistence and time travel need a separate snapshot path.
Rc-based state cannot cross threads, so moving shared state to a web worker or server-side rendering requires an explicit serializable protocol.
